concept: Cost-based ranker and the plan cache (8.3+)
summary: Source-anchored research for Cost-based ranker and the plan cache (8.3+). Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The plan cache does not survive mongod restart or shutdown. Collection DDL, including creating, deleting, or hiding an index, clears the relevant collection's plan cache; cache-state changes must therefore be considered when comparing planning behavior. (low confidence)

SERVER-115645 reports that a short estimation trial can yield zero parent productivity under LIMIT or blocking operations despite productive children. This is an implementation limitation to investigate, not proof that a particular deployed 8.3 patch is affected. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-06)

Starting in 8.3, the default for eligible queries is multi-planning with CBR backup: after a short trial, selection rules decide whether multi-planning continues or CBR ranks candidate plans. This does not mean CBR replaces the multi-planner for every query. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

CBR evaluates plan nodes using a cost function and cardinality estimates and selects the lowest overall estimated cost. The v8.3 explain reference defines costEstimate in abstract cost units, so interpreting that value as a monetary chargeback amount is unsupported. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/

The v8.3 explain reference marks costEstimate, cardinalityEstimate, numKeysEstimate, numDocsEstimate, and estimatesMetadata as new in 8.3.3. Do not assume these detailed fields are available in every 8.3 patch. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

explain() ignores existing cache entries for execution and does not create a new cache entry. Its isCached field can identify whether a candidate matches a cached plan; that flag alone does not demonstrate that the explain execution reused the cached plan. Inspect $planCacheStats separately. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/

The documented cache lifecycle has Missing, Inactive, and Active states. An Inactive entry is a placeholder; an Active entry can supply a plan, and a performance check can return it to Inactive. (high confidence)

planCacheShapeHash depends on the plan-cache query shape, whereas planCacheKey also depends on indexes available to support that shape. Index changes can therefore change the key without changing the shape hash. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-27)

SERVER-117635 describes reusing and pruning the existing multi-planner stage after CBR selection to obtain cache insertion work measurements. SERVER-121644 explicitly limits that completed work to the no-mp-results fallback and requests similar support for the cost-based selection strategy; this is not evidence that every CBR strategy has identical reuse behavior. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-07) Sources: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-117635 ; https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-121644

The University of Sydney FPTP study evaluated MongoDB 7.0.1 and observed index-scan preference that could produce plans taking more than twice the optimal runtime. This is historical motivation for optimizer analysis, not evidence that 8.3 CBR has the same regression or eliminates it. (low confidence)

Percona's July 30, 2026 announcement describes its own 8.3 release as a technical preview and describes the short multi-planning trial followed by estimated CBR selection. It provides corroborating implementation context, not an independent workload benchmark of Atlas savings. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-30)
Both the classic multi-planner and CBR store the chosen plan in the query plan cache for reuse by subsequent queries with the same plan-cache query shape. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

serverStatus documents metrics.query.cbr.count as CBR uses, choseWinningPlan as CBR winning-plan selections, and micros as ranking time including sampling. It also exposes failed-cost-estimation and tied-cost counters; these counters are documented as new in 8.3.3. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)
